headline_marked: Ishraque Hossain [[resigns as state minister]] to lead anti-drug drive
headline: Ishraque Hossain resigns as state minister to lead anti-drug drive
summary: The State Minister for Liberation War Affairs stepped down voluntarily, citing a need to focus on drug campaigns in Dhaka-6 following controversy over a firearm.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has announced his voluntary resignation to focus on an anti-drug campaign in the Dhaka-6 constituency and surrounding areas.
The move follows social media backlash after videos surfaced showing him carrying a firearm during an 'anti-drug' operation near the Ghuntighar railway crossing in Gandaria, Dhaka.
Ishraque defended the operation, stating that the area had become a drug hub and that six people were detained and handed over to police with seized evidence.
He clarified that he held his licensed weapon for personal protection and denied any wrongdoing, though he apologized to anyone hurt by the operation.
Addressing a press conference at the Jatiya Press Club, he rejected reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed him to step down, calling the resignation his own choice.
Ishraque argued that the focus of media coverage shifted from the drug campaign to his firearm, and emphasized the need to target main suppliers rather than street-level distributors.
He stated that the Prime Minister agreed to his request to concentrate on constituency-level work and public concerns.
The former minister maintained that the operation was conducted in coordination with local law enforcement and was a response to public demand for action against criminal activities.
caption:
From state minister to anti-drug campaigner. Ishraque Hossain resigns following a firearm controversy.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has announced his voluntary resignation to focus on an anti-drug campaign in the Dhaka-6 constituency and surrounding areas.

The move follows social media backlash after videos surfaced showing him carrying a firearm during an 'anti-drug' operation near the Ghuntighar railway crossing in Gandaria, Dhaka.

Ishraque defended the operation, stating that the area had become a drug hub and that six people were detained and handed over to police with seized evidence.

He clarified that he held his licensed weapon for personal protection and denied any wrongdoing, though he apologized to anyone hurt by the operation.

Addressing a press conference at the Jatiya Press Club, he rejected reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed him to step down, calling the resignation his own choice.

Ishraque argued that the focus of media coverage shifted from the drug campaign to his firearm, and emphasized the need to target main suppliers rather than street-level distributors.

He stated that the Prime Minister agreed to his request to concentrate on constituency-level work and public concerns.

The former minister maintained that the operation was conducted in coordination with local law enforcement and was a response to public demand for action against criminal activities.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com
